text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG

- Parents of schoolchildren in Brandenburg file lawsuit in German constitutional court against state school authorities for state government's refusal to introduce religion classes as part of regular school ciriculum.

- Finance Minister Theo Waigel demands cabinet reshuffle this year. Departure of Post Minister Wolfgang Poetsch (CSU) at end of this year when Post Ministry dissolved at core of demands. Waigel plans to discuss matter with Chancellor Helmut Kohl.
- Waigel plans to apply pressure on European Union to lower Germany's contributions to Brussels. He wants to lower Bonn's annual contributions by about seven billion marks.
- Defence Minister Volker Ruehe wants to reduce size of special air transport fleet available for political leaders by selling three of the nine planes available. Measure aimed at cost saving.
- Thyssen and Krupp examine possibility of closer cooperation. A complete merger of two steel companies possible.
HANDELSBLATT
- Waigel wants to play less to EU. Bonn plans concrete steps to drastically reduce Germany's payments to Brussels.
- Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel says debate in the cabinet about continuing draft for German army is not serious enough to endanger the coalition.
- SPD chairman Oskar Lafontaine and Lower Saxony premier Gerhard Schroeder reject government's tax cutting plans, saying the state can not afford to cut taxes as sharply as government wants.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Waigel says cabinet should be reshuffled this year.
- Waigel wants to cut EU payments by seven billion marks per year.
- Lafontaine urges that successor to German President Roman Herzog (CDU) should come from SPD, which has only had one federal president.

- New dispute about Germany army in Bosnia. A reserve officer of the army being investigated for making defamatory comments before being stationed on peacekeeping mission in Bosnia. The officer was suspended.
DIE WELT
- Waigel calls for reshuffled cabinet.
- Kinkel wants to maintain draft.
- Summer retail sales strong, retailers report.
